ov: More than 2,400 species of soft-bodied beetles, many of which glow, mostly at twilight, to attract mates. All glow as larvae, a warning that they taste bad. They live in temperate and tropical regions, often in marshes and damp woods where their larvae find food.
df: Larvae hunt other larvae, snails and slugs; adults vary: some hunt, some eat pollen or nectar, and some never eat.
fx: Female Photuris fireflies copy another species’ flash code to lure its males, then eat them.
In parts of Southeast Asia and the Great Smoky Mountains, whole groups flash in sync.
